summary: 纳米比亚钻石矿区出土了一艘载有铜锭和金币的沉船。考古学家把铸币年代、货物用途和里斯本残存的航海档案拼在一起，将它与 1533 年失踪的葡萄牙商船 Bom Jesus 联系起来。
logic: 矿工发现沉船与铜锭、金币
用钱币和航海档案辨认船名
借海岸与残骸重建失事经过
船员可能的去向与钻石海岸的来历

paragraphs.brief: 风暴把逐富商船带向沉没
sentences: History rarely unfolds like a fable.
历史很少像寓言那样展开。

But consider this: A 16th-century Portuguese trading vessel, carrying a fortune in gold and ivory and bound for a famed spice port on the coast of India, is blown far off course by a fierce storm while trying to round the southern tip of Africa.
但请设想，一艘十六世纪的葡萄牙商船满载黄金和象牙，驶向印度海岸著名的香料港，却在试图绕过非洲南端时被狂风吹得远离航线。
Days later, battered and broken, the ship founders on a mysterious, fogbound coast sprinkled with more than a hundred million carats of diamonds, a cruel mockery of the sailors’ dreams of riches.
几天后，伤痕累累的船沉没在一片神秘的雾岸，那里散布着超过一亿克拉的钻石，仿佛在残酷地嘲弄水手们的发财梦。
None of the castaways ever return home.
这些遇难者没有一人重返故乡。
paragraphs.gist: 一艘载着黄金和象牙、驶向印度的葡萄牙商船绕行非洲南端时遭风暴偏航，最终沉没在遍布钻石的海岸，没有船员回到故乡。

paragraphs.brief: 地质学家从铜锭发现沉船
sentences: This improbable yarn would have been lost forever had it not been for the astonishing discovery in April 2008 of a shipwreck in the beach sands of the Sperrgebiet—the fabulously rich and famously off-limits De Beers diamond-mining lease near the mouth of the Orange River on Namibia’s southern coast.
这个几乎令人难以置信的故事本会永远失传，直到 2008 年 4 月，人们在纳米比亚南岸奥兰治河口附近的斯佩尔禁区海滩发现沉船，那是戴比尔斯公司一块盛产钻石、严禁外人进入的租采区。
A company geologist working in mining area U-60 came across what at first he took to be a perfectly round half sphere of rock.
一位在 U-60 矿区工作的公司地质学家发现了一件起初看似完美半球形岩石的东西。
Curious, he picked it up and immediately realized it was a copper ingot.
他好奇地捡起它，立刻看出那是一块铜锭。
A strange trident-shaped mark on its weathered surface turned out to be the hallmark of Anton Fugger, one of Renaissance Europe’s wealthiest financiers.
铜锭风化表面的奇异三叉标记，后来被认作欧洲文艺复兴时期巨富安东·富格尔的商号印记。
The ingot was the type traded for spices in the Indies in the first half of the 16th century.
这种铜锭在十六世纪上半叶曾用来在东印度群岛换取香料。
paragraphs.gist: 2008 年，纳米比亚钻石矿的一名地质学家在沙中拾到带三叉标记的铜锭，由其商号和用途，为十六世纪商船遗址提供了第一条线索。

paragraphs.brief: 铜锭、武器与各国金币
sentences: Archaeologists would later find a staggering 22 tons of these ingots beneath the sand, as well as cannon and swords, ivory and astrolabes, muskets and chain mail—thousands of artifacts in all.
考古学家后来在沙下发现了足足二十二吨这种铜锭，还有大炮、剑、象牙、星盘、火枪和锁子甲等数千件文物。

And gold, of course, fistfuls of gold: more than 2,000 beautiful, heavy coins— mainly Spanish excelentes bearing the likenesses of Ferdinand and Isabella, but also a smattering of Venetian, Moorish, French, and other coinage, as well as exquisite portugueses with the coat of arms of King João III.
当然还有大把黄金：两千多枚精美厚重的金币以铸有斐迪南和伊莎贝拉肖像的西班牙 excelentes 为主，也有少量威尼斯、摩尔、法国等地的货币，以及铸有若昂三世纹章的葡萄牙金币。
paragraphs.gist: 沙下出土了二十二吨铜锭、武器、航海仪器和两千多枚金币，既有大量西班牙金币，也有葡萄牙及其他地区的铸币。

paragraphs.brief: 沉船及完整货物的罕见价值
sentences: It is by far the oldest shipwreck ever found on the coast of sub-Saharan Africa, and the richest.
这是迄今在撒哈拉以南非洲海岸发现的最古老的沉船，也是最富的。

Its dollar value is anyone’s guess, but none of its treasures have fired the imaginations of the world’s archaeologists as much as the wreck itself: a Portuguese East Indiaman from the 1530s, the heart of the age of discovery, with its cargo of treasure and trade goods intact, having lain untouched and unsuspected in these sands for nearly 500 years.
没人能估出它值多少钱，但最让各地考古学家心动的正是沉船本身：这艘十六世纪三十年代大航海时代的葡萄牙远洋商船，满载财宝与贸易商品，在沙中不为人知地沉睡了近五百年。
paragraphs.gist: 最让考古学家振奋的是沉船本身，这艘十六世纪三十年代的葡萄牙远洋商船连同货物在沙中保存近五百年，未遭扰动。

paragraphs.brief: 难得的科学发掘机会
sentences: “This is a priceless opportunity,” says Francisco Alves, the doyen of Portuguese maritime archaeologists and the head of nautical archaeology under the Ministry of Culture.
葡萄牙海事考古界前辈、文化部航海考古负责人弗朗西斯科·阿尔韦斯说：“这是个无价的机会。”
“We know so little about these great old ships.
我们对这些昔日巨轮知之甚少。
This is only the second one ever excavated by archaeologists.
这只是考古学家发掘的第二艘同类船只。
All the others were plundered by treasure hunters.”
其他船都已被寻宝者洗劫。
paragraphs.gist: 海事考古学家阿尔韦斯称这是难得的研究机会，因为同类古船大多早被寻宝者洗劫，这只是第二艘由考古学家发掘的实例。

paragraphs.brief: 钻石禁区如何保护遗址
sentences: Treasure hunters are never going to be a problem here, not in the middle of one of the world’s most jealously guarded diamond mines, on a coast whose very name— Sperrgebiet—means “forbidden zone” in German.
在这里，寻宝者几乎不可能构成威胁：沉船位于世界上守卫最严密的钻石矿之一，连海岸的德文名字 Sperrgebiet 都意为“禁区”。

Far from plundering, officials at De Beers and in the Namibian government, who work the lease as a joint venture called Namdeb, suspended their operations around the wreck site, called in a team of archaeologists, and for a few gloriously diverting weeks mined history instead of diamonds.
戴比尔斯和纳米比亚政府以 Namdeb 合资开矿，他们没有掠夺遗址，反而暂停附近的开采，召来考古队，在那几个格外有趣的星期里从挖钻石转为发掘历史。
paragraphs.gist: 沉船恰在严密看守的钻石禁区内，矿业公司与纳米比亚政府暂停附近采矿、请考古学家进场，使遗址免遭盗掘。

paragraphs.brief: 船体结构与海上日常的线索
sentences: It will take scholars years to study the wealth of material gleaned from the Diamond Shipwreck, as it has come to be called.
学者们将花数年研究这艘被称为“钻石沉船”的古船所留下的丰富材料。
“So much is unknown,” says Filipe Vieira de Castro, the Portuguese-born coordinator of the nautical archaeology program at Texas A&M University.
得克萨斯农工大学航海考古项目协调人、出生于葡萄牙的菲利佩·维埃拉·德·卡斯特罗说：“未知的事情太多了。”
Castro has spent more than ten years studying Portuguese trading vessels, or naus, lately developing computer models based on the slender archaeological pickings available.
卡斯特罗研究这种称为 nau 的葡萄牙商船已有十多年，最近还依据为数不多的考古遗存建立了计算机模型。

“This wreck will give us new insights into everything from hull design, rigging, and how these ships evolved, to little day-to-day things such as how they cooked meals on board and what people brought with them on these great journeys.”
这艘沉船能让人了解船体设计、索具和船型演变，也能还原航海者如何做饭、远航随身带了什么等日常细节。
paragraphs.gist: 卡斯特罗原本只能凭零星证据建立船舶模型，而这批材料可让研究者同时了解船体、索具的设计演变和船上的饮食起居。

paragraphs.brief: 用档案重建失踪的航程
sentences: Already, some inspired detective work among the rare manuscripts and royal archives in Lisbon has cobbled together enough bits and pieces to tell the tale of a long-forgotten voyage and a vanished ship that turned out to be as rich in irony and allegory as it was in gold.
研究者像侦探般在里斯本的珍稀手稿与王室档案中拼凑线索，已经足以讲述这次久被遗忘的航行，而这艘失踪商船既满载黄金，也充满讽刺和寓意。
paragraphs.gist: 研究者拼合里斯本罕见手稿与王室档案中的零星线索，逐步还原了这次几乎被遗忘的航行。

paragraphs.brief: 印度船队从里斯本启航
sentences: The story begins on a fresh spring day in Lisbon—Friday, the seventh of March, 1533, to be exact—when the great naus of that year’s India fleet sailed grandly down the Tagus River and out into the broad Atlantic, flags and pennants flying and colorful silks and velvets draped from their towering castles.
故事始于里斯本一个清爽的春日，确切地说是 1533 年 3 月 7 日星期五，当年的印度船队沿塔霍河驶入大西洋，旗帜与三角旗飘扬，高耸的船楼垂挂着彩色丝绸和天鹅绒。
These were the pride of Portugal, the space shuttles of their day, off on a 15-month odyssey to bring back a fortune in pepper and spices from distant continents.
这些巨船是葡萄牙的骄傲，堪比当时的航天飞机，即将踏上十五个月的远航，从遥远大陆运回价值连城的胡椒和香料。

Goa, Cochin, Sofala, Mombasa, Zanzibar, Ternate: Storied places that once had been as remote as the stars were now familiar ports of call, part of the Portuguese vernacular, thanks to Portuguese ingenuity and cutting-edge technology.
果阿、科钦、索法拉、蒙巴萨、桑给巴尔、特尔纳特原本如星辰般遥远，依靠葡萄牙人的才智和先进技术，它们如今已成了人们耳熟能详的停靠港。
paragraphs.gist: 1533 年 3 月 7 日，葡萄牙船队从里斯本启航，计划用十五个月到海外运回胡椒和香料，昔日遥远的港口已成为熟悉的航点。

paragraphs.brief: “好耶稣号”与船上乘员
sentences: The outbound ships that sailed down the Tagus River in 1533 were sturdy and capable; two of them were brand-new and owned by the king himself.
1533 年沿塔霍河出航的船都坚固耐用，其中两艘是国王亲自拥有的新船。
One of these was the Bom Jesus—the Good Jesus—captained by one Dom Francisco de Noronha and carrying 300 or so sailors, soldiers, merchants, priests, nobles, and slaves.
其中一艘名为 Bom Jesus，意为“好耶稣号”，由弗朗西斯科·德·诺罗尼亚指挥，载着约三百名水手、士兵、商人、神父、贵族和奴隶。
paragraphs.gist: 出航船只中有两艘国王所有的新船，其中“好耶稣号”由诺罗尼亚指挥，载着水手、士兵、商人等约三百人。

paragraphs.brief: 里斯本灾难毁坏航运档案
sentences: PINNING A NAME and a story to an anonymous, five-centuries-old shipwreck found unexpectedly on a far-flung shore takes canny sleuthing and more than a little luck— particularly if it is thought likely to have been an early Portuguese wreck.
要为一艘在偏远海岸意外发现、沉没已五百年的无名船确定船名和身世，需要精明的查证，也少不了运气，尤其当它可能是早期的葡萄牙船时。

Although the Spanish Empire left mountains of paperwork in its wake, a catastrophic earthquake, tsunami, and fire in November 1755 virtually wiped Lisbon off the map and sent the Casa da India, the building that housed the vast majority of precious maps, charts, and shipping records, tumbling into the Tagus River.
尽管西班牙帝国留下大量文书，1755 年 11 月的一场强震及其引发的海啸和大火几乎将里斯本夷为平地。保存着绝大多数珍贵地图、海图和航运记录的印度事务院大楼也坍入了塔霍河。
paragraphs.gist: 为五百年前的无名沉船确定身份尤其困难，因为 1755 年里斯本地震、海啸及大火毁掉了存放航海记录的重要档案馆。

paragraphs.brief: 档案缺失迫使研究者另寻线索
sentences: “That left a huge hole in our history,” says Alexandre Monteiro, a maritime archaeologist and researcher who works with the Portuguese Ministry of Culture.
与葡萄牙文化部合作的海事考古学家亚历山大·蒙泰罗说：“这给我们的历史留下了一大片空白。”
“With no India archives left to peruse, one has to revert to other, more imaginative ways of finding information.”
“没有印度档案可供仔细研究，人们不得不回到其他更有想象力的查找信息的方法上。”
paragraphs.gist: 蒙泰罗指出，印度航线档案的毁失留下大片历史空白，研究人员只能另寻线索查证船只身份。

paragraphs.brief: 金币定年与铜锭指示航向
sentences: In this instance, a vital clue came from the coins found in abundance on the wreck— particularly those beautiful and rare portugueses of King João III.
这次调查的一条关键线索来自船上大量出土的硬币，尤其是若昂三世时期那些精美罕见的 portugueses 金币。
These were minted for only a few years, from 1525 to 1538, after which they were recalled, melted down, and never reissued.
这些金币仅在 1525 至 1538 年间铸造，之后被回收熔化，从未再次发行。
Finding so many sparkling new portugueses on the wreck is a strong indication that the ship sailed during this 13-year window in time.
船上这么多崭新的葡萄牙金币有力地说明，这艘船在那十三年间启航。
Moreover, the load of copper ingots suggests the ship was on its outward passage to India to buy spices rather than returning.
船载铜锭也表明它是在前往印度采购香料的去程，而非回程。
paragraphs.gist: 若昂三世金币的有限铸造时段把航期缩小到 1525 至 1538 年，而船载铜锭表明它正前往印度买香料。

paragraphs.brief: 船队纪事锁定可能船名
sentences: Although the complete Casa da India records are long gone, some tantalizing snippets remain in libraries and archives that survived the 1755 earthquake.
印度事务院的完整记录早已不存，但在经历 1755 年地震而幸存的图书馆和档案馆里，仍保留着一些引人探究的材料。
Among these are the Relações das Armadas, the so-called narratives of the fleets.
其中包括称为《船队纪事》的 Relações das Armadas。
A thorough study of the most complete narratives shows that 21 ships were lost on the way to India between 1525 and 1600.
对最完整的叙述进行彻底研究后发现，在1525年至1600年期间，有21艘船只在前往印度的途中丢失。
Only one of these went down anywhere near Namibia: the Bom Jesus, which sailed in 1533 and was “lost on the turn of the Cape of Good Hope.”
只有一艘是在纳米比亚附近失踪的，就是 1533 年出航、记作“在绕过好望角途中失踪”的“好耶稣号”。
paragraphs.gist: 幸存的船队纪事列出 1525 至 1600 年间驶往印度途中失事的二十一艘船，其中只有 1533 年的“好耶稣号”沉没地点接近纳米比亚。

paragraphs.brief: 王室信函解释西班牙金币
sentences: Another intriguing pointer to the Bom Jesus comes from a letter Monteiro unearthed in the royal archives.
蒙泰罗在王室档案中挖出的一封信，又提供了一条指向“好耶稣号”的线索。

Dated February 13, 1533, it reveals that King João had just sent a knight to Seville to pick up 20,000 crusadoes’ worth of gold from a consortium of businessmen who had invested in the fleet that was about to sail for India—the fleet that included the Bom Jesus.
信的日期是 1533 年 2 月 13 日，记载若昂国王刚派骑士前往塞维利亚，从为即将启航的印度船队投资的商人团体处领取价值两万克鲁扎多的黄金，这支船队就包括“好耶稣号”。
Archaeologists had been puzzled by the huge quantity of Spanish coins found among the wreckage—about 70 percent of the gold pieces were excelentes, unexpected for a Portuguese ship.
沉船金币中约七成是西班牙的 excelentes，这个葡萄牙船上出人意料的比例曾令考古学家十分费解。
“This letter would go a long way toward explaining that,” says Monteiro.
Monteiro说，“这封信将大大有助于解释这一点”。
“Spanish investors, it seems, had an unusually large stake in the 1533 fleet.”
“看来西班牙投资者在1533年船队中拥有非常大的利益。”
paragraphs.gist: 一封王室信函记载西班牙投资人为这支船队出资，这解释了为何葡萄牙沉船上约七成金币竟是西班牙铸造的。

paragraphs.brief: 纪念画册留下沉船图像
sentences: A rare 16th-century tome called the Memória das Armadas even offers a tantalizing glimpse of the Bom Jesus.
一本名叫《船队纪念册》的十六世纪罕见古籍，甚至让人得以一窥“好耶稣号”的模样。

Issued as a commemorative volume, a sort of Renaissance-era coffee-table book, it contains illustrations of all the fleets that sailed for India each year after Vasco da Gama pioneered the route in 1497.
这部纪念画册颇像文艺复兴时代的案头图书，收录了达·伽马 1497 年开辟航线后每年驶往印度的历支船队插画。
Among the pictures for 1533 is a vignette of two rigged masts under full sail disappearing into the waves and the words “Bom Jesus” together with a simple epitaph: perdido—lost.
1533 年的画页中，两根挂满风帆的桅杆正在浪中消失，旁边写着“好耶稣号”和简短的悼词 perdido，意为“失踪”。
paragraphs.gist: 十六世纪的一部船队纪念画册为认定船名再添佐证，1533 年的插图在沉入浪中的船桅旁直接写着船名及“失踪”一词。

paragraphs.brief: 从风暴记录推测触礁经过
sentences: So what did happen?
发生什么事了？
It seems that four months or so after its grand departure from Lisbon, the first fleet of 1533 was struck and scattered by a huge storm.
约在隆重离开里斯本四个月后，1533 年的首支船队似乎遇上了将各船冲散的大风暴。
Details are sketchy.
详情已难考证。
An account of the voyage by Captain Dom João Pereira, the fleet’s commander, has been lost.
船队指挥官若昂·佩雷拉船长的航行报告已经失传。
All that remains is a clerk’s acknowledgement that the report was received and a mention that the Bom Jesus disappeared in wild weather somewhere off the cape.
只剩一名文书确认收到报告的记录，还提到“好耶稣号”在海角附近的恶劣天气中消失。

It is easy to envision what might have happened next: The storm-battered ship was caught up in the powerful winds and currents that surge along the southwest African coast and was driven helplessly northward for hundreds of miles.
不难想象随后可能发生的事：饱受风暴摧残的船被非洲西南岸的强风和海流裹挟，无法自主地向北漂了数百英里。
As the windswept scrub of the Namib Desert hove into view, the doomed nau struck an outcrop of rock about 150 yards from shore.
风中的纳米布沙漠灌丛进入视野时，这艘命途已尽的船撞上离岸约一百五十码的岩礁。
The shuddering blow broke off a big chunk of the stern, spilling tons of copper ingots into the sea and sending the Bom Jesus to its grave.
剧烈的撞击折断了船尾的一大块，成吨铜锭落海，“好耶稣号”就此沉没。
paragraphs.gist: 史料仅证实船队出发约四个月后遭风暴打散，研究者推测“好耶稣号”被风浪向北推行，近岸触礁后船尾断裂、铜锭落海。

paragraphs.brief: 挡海墙里的考古现场
sentences: FAST-FORWARD five centuries to a maritime archaeology site that feels slightly surreal.
镜头快进五个世纪，眼前是一处略带超现实感的海事考古现场。

A knot of researchers in hats and sunscreen are excavating a sunken ship that rests some 20 feet below sea level, the Atlantic Ocean held back by a massive earthen retaining wall that leaks a bit along its base.
一群戴帽子、涂防晒霜的研究者正在发掘海平面下约二十英尺的沉船，一道巨大的土质挡水墙挡住大西洋，墙脚略有渗漏。
Closed-circuit television cameras, set up around the perimeter of the site, monitor everyone’s movements—a reminder that for all the excitement of the find, this is still a diamond mine.
闭路电视摄像头在现场周围安装，监测每个人的行动，提醒人们，由于发现的一切令人兴奋，这里仍然是钻石矿。
And a rich one, where loose diamonds could well be mingled in the sands the archaeologists are brushing away.
而且这还是座富矿，考古学家扫去的沙中完全可能混着散落的钻石。
paragraphs.gist: 五世纪后，考古人员在挡海土墙内、海平面下约二十英尺处开挖，矿区监控仍密切记录动作，因为遗址沙层中可能混有钻石。

paragraphs.brief: 沉重铜锭保存船体残骸
sentences: “If it hadn’t been for those copper ingots weighing everything down, there would be nothing left here to find,” says Bruno Werz, director of the Southern African Institute of Maritime Archaeology, who was called in from Cape Town to assist with the excavation.
“要不是那些铜锭压住了所有东西，这里就什么也留不下了。”南部非洲海洋考古研究所所长布鲁诺·韦尔茨说。他是从开普敦受邀前来协助发掘的。
“Five centuries of storms and waves would have washed everything away.”
“五个世纪的暴风雨和海浪本可以冲走一切。”
paragraphs.gist: 韦尔茨认为，正是沉重的铜锭压住了遗存，否则近五百年的风暴与海浪早会将它们冲走。

paragraphs.brief: 三维扫描重建解体过程
sentences: Werz and a team of researchers have been poring over the wreckage, measuring, photographing, scanning the site millimeter by millimeter with a state-of-the-art, three-dimensional laser scanner.
韦尔茨与同事仔细检查残骸，测量、拍照，用先进的三维激光扫描仪逐毫米扫描遗址。

They are trying, among other things, to piece together the ship’s final harrowing moments, which would not have been pretty—the mangled remains of the hull and forecastle and a tangle of sails, spars, and rigging sloshing about in the swell, drifting north with the current and probably breaking apart as it went.
他们希望重建遇难前最后的惊险时刻：船体与艏楼支离破碎，帆、桅杆和索具纠作一团，在浪中颠簸，随海流北漂，可能沿途继续解体。
Mine workers found a huge wooden rigging block three miles farther up the coast.
矿工们在沿海向北三英里处找到了一块巨大的木制索具滑轮。
paragraphs.gist: 研究团队逐毫米扫描残骸，结合更北面找到的大型木制滑轮，推测断裂的船体和索具怎样随浪漂散。

paragraphs.brief: 船上人员的下落成谜
sentences: And what of the people on board, Dom Francisco and the rest?
那么，船长弗朗西斯科和其余船上的人怎么样了？
paragraphs.gist: 船只最后的遭遇渐有眉目，叙事转而追问船长和其他船上人员的命运。

paragraphs.brief: 登岸机会取决于风浪
sentences: “A winter storm along this coast is no joke,” says Dieter Noli, the mine’s resident archaeologist, who has lived and worked along this stretch of the Namib Desert for more than ten years.
在这片纳米布沙漠生活工作逾十年的矿区考古学家迪特尔·诺利说，这段海岸的冬季风暴绝非儿戏。
“It would have been nasty, with winds of over 80 miles an hour and a huge breaking surf.
当时若有时速逾八十英里的风和巨大的拍岸浪，情况会非常险恶。
Getting ashore would have been just about impossible.
上岸几乎是不可能的

On the other hand, if the storm had blown itself out and the ship wallowed ashore on one of those quiet, fog-shrouded days we also get around here, well, now that opens up all kinds of interesting possibilities.”
另一方面，如果风暴已经平息，船在当地也常有的安静雾日里颠簸着漂近岸，情况便会有许多耐人寻味的可能。
paragraphs.gist: 当地考古学家指出，冬季巨浪中登岸几乎不可能，但若风暴已经过去，船在平静多雾时漂近岸边，船员或有生机。

paragraphs.brief: 遗骨与随身物品提示有人上岸
sentences: That may have happened.
这可能已经发生了。

Although the discovery of human toe bones in a shoe found pinned beneath a mass of timbers indicates that at least one person did not survive, those were the only human remains recovered from the wreck.
虽然在被钉在一大批木材下的鞋中发现人的脚趾骨，表明至少有一人没有存活下来，但从残骸中找到的只有这些遗骸。
And few personal possessions were found among the artifacts.
在文物中发现的个人物品很少。
These facts lead archaeologists to believe that despite the breakup of the ship along the surf line, many if not most of those aboard made it to land.
这些情况使考古学家相信，尽管船在碎浪区解体，仍可能有许多、甚至多数船员上了岸。
paragraphs.gist: 鞋里的趾骨证明至少一人遇难，但遗址没有发现其他人骨，私人物品也少，因此考古学家推测许多人可能成功上岸。

paragraphs.brief: 沙漠海岸几无获救机会
sentences: And then what?
然后怎么办？
This is one of the most inhospitable places on Earth, an uninhabited wasteland of sand and scrub stretching for hundreds of miles.
此处是地球上最不适于居住的地方之一，无人居住的沙地和灌丛延伸数百英里。
It was winter.
当时正值冬季。
They were cold and wet, exhausted and bereft.
他们又冷又湿，筋疲力尽，一无所有。
There was no hope of rescue or a search party, for nobody in the outside world knew they were alive, let alone where to start looking.
救援或搜索队是没有希望的，因为外面的世界没有人知道他们还活着，更别提从哪里开始寻找了。
Nor was any ship likely to pass this way by chance; they were far off the trade routes.
任何船只也不可能偶然通过这条路；它们离贸易路线很远。
As for somehow getting back to Portugal—well, the crew might as well have been shipwrecked on Mars.
至于回到葡萄牙，他们所处的地方简直和在火星上遇难一样遥远。
paragraphs.gist: 即使登岸，幸存者面对的也是冬季荒凉的沙漠，外界不知道他们的下落，附近又偏离商船航线，很难获救。

paragraphs.brief: 附近河水与海岸食物
sentences: All the same, things needn’t necessarily have ended badly for the castaways, according to Noli.
不过诺利认为，这些海难幸存者的结局未必一定悲惨。
The Orange River lay only 16 miles to the south of the wreck, a source of fresh water whose bloom they might have noticed as they drifted by its mouth.
奥兰治河就在沉船以南十六英里处，是淡水来源，船员从河口附近漂过时，也许已留意到淡水入海形成的水色变化。
And there was plenty of food about: shellfish, seabird eggs, and loads of desert land snails.
有很多食物：贝类，海鸟蛋，和大量的沙漠蜗牛。
paragraphs.gist: 诺利认为幸存者仍可能找到给养，因为沉船以南不远便有提供淡水的奥兰治河，海岸也有贝类、鸟蛋和沙漠蜗牛。

paragraphs.brief: 可能遇见当地狩猎采集者
sentences: What’s more, the Portuguese could have met the local survival experts.
更何况，葡萄牙人本可以见见当地的生存专家。
Winter was the season when hunter-gatherers known today as Bushmen ventured north along this shore in hopes of finding the carcasses of the southern right whales that occasionally wash ashore here.
冬季，今天称为布须曼人的狩猎采集者会沿这段海岸向北寻找偶尔被冲上岸的南露脊鲸尸体。
paragraphs.gist: 冬季当地狩猎采集者会沿海向北寻找搁浅鲸鱼的尸体，葡萄牙幸存者可能因此遇到熟悉这一环境的人。

paragraphs.brief: 以交易换取和平相处的机会
sentences: How the Portuguese fared in these encounters would have been up to them, says Noli.
诺利说，葡萄牙人在这些接触中会有怎样的遭遇，取决于他们自己的做法。
“If they had the wit to trade rather than try to take, there is no reason to believe everybody wouldn’t get along.
如果他们足够明智，选择交易而非强取，那就没有理由认为双方不能和睦相处。
The few small bands of hunter-gatherers along the river had no population-resource pressures to contend with, and so no reason to be aggressive to the newcomers.
沿河的少数猎人-采集者没有人口资源压力，因此没有理由对新来者采取侵略行动。
On the contrary, a big, strapping Portuguese dom could well have been seen as an attractive prospect for a son-in-law.”
相反，当地人很可能觉得，一位身材高大健壮的葡萄牙贵族会是个不错的女婿人选。
paragraphs.gist: 诺利推测，当地小群体的资源压力不大，若葡萄牙人愿意交易，他们或能和平相处，甚至通过婚姻建立联系。

paragraphs.brief: 逐富者不识岸上钻石
sentences: Whatever their final fate, the survivors of the Bom Jesus had no inkling of the exquisite irony with which their prayers, uttered so long ago in Lisbon, had been answered.
不论最后命运如何，“好耶稣号”的幸存者都不会知道，多年前在里斯本许下的祈愿竟以如此巧妙而讽刺的方式得到回应。
They’d set off on a great journey in search of riches, pledging altars and icons for favor and success.
他们远航寻求财富，曾许诺献上祭坛和圣像，以祈求庇佑与成功。

Now here they were, delivered onto a shore of unimaginable wealth—a 185-mile stretch of desert so fantastically rich in high-quality diamonds that in the early 1900s an explorer named Ernst Reuning made a wager with a companion about the amount of time it would take to fill a tin cup with gems found loose in the sand.
如今他们竟被送到一片财富难以想象的海岸：这段长一百八十五英里的沙漠富产优质钻石，以至于在二十世纪初，探险家恩斯特·罗伊宁曾与同伴打赌，看捡满一锡杯散落沙中的宝石需花多久。
The job took all of ten minutes.
结果只花了十分钟。
paragraphs.gist: 幸存者并不知道，逐富之旅把他们送到了钻石极其丰富的海岸，几个世纪后有人在沙中十分钟就捡满一杯宝石。

paragraphs.brief: 河流与寒流运来钻石
sentences: For long ages the great river had been washing millions, even billions of diamonds down from deposits as far as 1,700 miles inland.
漫长的岁月里，这条大河把数百万乃至数十亿颗钻石一路冲向下游；它们来自远在内陆 1,700 英里处的矿床。
Only the hardest, most brilliant, gem-quality stones, some weighing hundreds of carats, survived the journey.
只有最坚硬、最璀璨、达到宝石级的钻石能承受这段旅程，其中一些重达数百克拉。
They spilled into the Atlantic at the river’s mouth and were washed up the coast, borne by the same cold current that would one day sweep the Bom Jesus to its death.
钻石从河口流入大西洋，再被寒流沿海岸推送上岸，后来将“好耶稣号”推向覆没的正是这股洋流。
paragraphs.gist: 河流把遥远内陆的钻石带到海口，耐磨的宝石再被寒流送上岸，而同一股寒流后来也把“好耶稣号”推向覆没。

points: 纳米比亚钻石矿区出土了一艘载有铜锭和金币的沉船。考古学家把铸币年代、货物用途和里斯本残存的航海档案拼在一起，将它与 1533 年失踪的葡萄牙商船 Bom Jesus 联系起来。
矿区意外发现沉船 → 盘点铜锭与金币 → 用航线及残存档案辨认船名 → 推测失事经过

lead: Five centuries ago a ship loaded with gold wrecked off a beach laden with diamonds.
五百年前，一艘满载黄金的船在一片遍布钻石的海滩外失事了。
